new_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Quality
new_roles.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.

 

For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.

At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.

 

We are looking for a S **r. Manager, Quality** to join our team in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This role will report to **Director of Quality** and based in **Newark, Delaware. This is a fully on-site, in office role 5 days a week** .

 

**Role and Responsibilities:**

* Ensure 100% Quality assurance at the Skid line manufacturing through inspection, testing, and sub-component testing/inspection. Assist in hiring personnel needed to support this effort.

* Partner with Install Quality team (field) to understand real time (daily) what items are escaping the plant and instituting immediate mitigation plans including addressing any inventory in the pipeline not yet installed.

* Implement permanent corrective actions working with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply chain, or SQE as per relevance on each issue.

* Provide quality input into the new equipment being purchased for the scaling of Delaware manufacturing. Include inputs for quality assurance into equipment design, and verification of process steps. Understand and provide input into the planned operation, what can be bypassed, maintenance plans, calibration or drift of the equipment, automation that can fail and be undetected leading to quality escapes.

* Participate and understand results from testing in the plant; Functional test, Tommy test, FIT, etc. Drive pareto of failures to help cross functional problem solving of test failures.

* Implement a 100% functional test (new) on skid final product assembly; electrical continuity, communications integrity, piping assurance, start up simulation, etc. to assure 100% QA prior to shipping to customer.

* Ensure skid components and systems have latest FW revision prior to shipping to the W/H, or out of W/H to field.

* Work with CIG and Manufacturing Engr, and NPI to implement workload being removed from the customer install side and being moved into skid assembly. Provide oversight to ensure best quality achievement; ensure work instructions are clear, operators trained, workstations have proper tools, and judgement criteria.

* Collaborate with Supplier Quality / Suppliers to achieve zero-defect flow (“dock-to-stock”) for all purchased, contract manufacture parts, materials, and Bloom Energy manufactured parts.

* Drive component and design failures back to the earliest point of detection in the process.

* Ensure manufacturing process have Control plans with CTQ, and POA built in to each station.

* Work collaboratively with Design teams to DFM, through a “registration system”, and Pokeyoke assembly methods for highest quality assurance.

* Drive test excellence in the manufacturing plan to ensure that equipment and test stations are certified with robust qualification programs, that are documented and controlled for changes with proper accuracy and gage R&R techniques.

* Drive yield task forces to achieve company wide targets at each manufacturing point under this scope, with cross functional teams driving top pareto issues to RCCA.

* Ensure early engagement with the product engineering team to teach and perform early stage risk assessments (DFMEA et.al.)

* Design for manufacturability and reliability improvements during the early design stages of product development.

* Work with Engineering NPI and the manufacturing engineering teams to perform PFMEA, write work instructions, and establish quality check-points to guarantee zero-defect quality in production.

* Develop and implement formal, comprehensive process documentation including process flow diagrams, Process FMEAs, process control plans, operations method Sheets, manufacturing quality charts (MQCs) and etc.

* Lead critical problem solving task forces with emphasis on cross functional inputs, accountability, time to RCCA, and ensurance of mitigation of inventory, or field units at risk.

* Troubleshoot product issues by reviewing engineering drawings and design requirements. Drive a rigorous resolution process for product quality, reliability and design issues.

* Perform data-driven root cause failure analyses for design, manufacturing, and administrative problems.

* Perform process audits to monitor, continuously improve, and sustain superior product quality.

* Demonstrate the ability to interface and work collaboratively across departments internally and with suppliers and customers, (including Purchasing, Quality, R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Marketing and Finance), while building strong and cooperative working relationships.

* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Establish and govern site COPQ metrics (scrap, rework, sorting, and warranty risk); lead cross-functional yield-improvement blitzes targeting measurable cost reductions and scrap minimization.

* Process Capability & Zero-Defect Mentality: Drive process capability (C\_p / C\_{pk} \ge 1.33) across critical-to-quality (CTQ) operations (welding, brazing, ceramic stack assembly, plumbing/gas-delivery, and electrical integration).

 

**Skills and Experience:**

* More than 10 years of increasing responsibility in the areas of Quality, and Manufacturing .

* Experience implementing company-wide ISO 9001 procedures and TS16949 standards and related process documentation. Possess working knowledge of process capability and control requirements, methods and systems.

* Demonstrated track record of building, restructuring, or significantly scaling a manufacturing quality team during rapid production ramp-up

* Proven successful application of multi-discipline engineering problem solving techniques.

* Understand the critical elements of modern Manufacturing Statistical Process Control, (e.g., practical working knowledge and experience with SPC, Process Capability, Cp, Cpk, etc.)

* Understand the critical elements of modern Reliability Engineering, (e.g., MCF, MTBF, MTT, etc.)

* Certification in a recognized problem-solving methodology such as six-sigma Black Belt, 8D, or Global Problem Solving.

* Strong verbal/active listening/written communications.

* Demonstrate planning and leadership skills.

* Expert with metrology, calibration, and Gage R & R’s.

* Ability to train in Quality System Auditing.

* Fluent in product phase-gate, NPI and technology transfer.

* Expertise in applying PPAP, First Article Inspections (FAI) and Reports).

* Strong critical thinking, analytical skills, and problem solving.

* Ability to effectively work within a very intense, dynamic, fast-paced, and demanding work environment.

* Familiarity with industry codes and quality standards applicable to clean power systems (ISO 9001:2015 required; working knowledge of ASME, NFPA, or UL standards preferred).

* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality / Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) and ASQ Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) alongside CQE and Six Sigma Black Belt.

* Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite and statistical software.

* Possess a passion for excellence.

* Unrestricted willingness to travel to all regions. Travel may be up to 25% of time.

* BS, MS or PhD in Mechanical/Material Science/Chemical/Electrical/Systems Engineering.

* Direct experience managing high-temperature fluidics/gas delivery, welding/brazing, ceramic integration, power electronics, or structural enclosures is a strong plus.

 

Bloom Energy is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We are committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants, will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability. Bloom Energy makes reasonable accommodations, consistent with applicable laws, for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant or employee with a disability, who can perform the essential job functions, unless undue hardship would result.

 

At Bloom Energy, we are committed to supporting the well-being of our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees includes competitive Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with a large employer contribution, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, generous Mental Health Support services, Legal services, virtual Physical Therapy access, and Fertility & Family Forming benefits.

Bloom Energy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The total compensation for this position includes standard company benefits and is based on various factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience.

**Salary Ranges:**
==================

$149,300.00 - $214,700.00

new_roles.title: Director, Central Laboratory Operations
new_roles.description:
By clicking the “Apply” button, I understand that my employment application process with Takeda will commence and that the information I provide in my application will be processed in line with Takeda’s Privacy Notice and Terms of Use. I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.

**Job Description**
-------------------

OBJECTIVES/PURPOSE

 

* Builds and leads Takeda’s new Central Laboratory Operations group, defining the vision, operating model, organizational design, capabilities, and ways of working required to deliver enterprise technical and operational oversight of central laboratory services across global clinical development programs.
* Establishes the foundational infrastructure for central laboratory oversight, including processes, vendor strategy, systems, and metrics, so that central laboratory solutions are technically sound, operationally executable, globally compliant, and inspection-ready from study design through database lock and study closeout.
* Provides leadership of the Sample Management group, ensuring its in-trial activities interface effectively with central laboratory operations. Biorepository and biobank activities are out of scope for this role.
* Partners with Clinical Science, Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Procurement, and external laboratory providers to deliver consistent, scalable central laboratory capabilities across the portfolio.

ACCOUNTABILITIES

 

**Building the Central Laboratory Operations Group (primary focus)**

* Define and execute the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap to stand up the Central Laboratory Operations group, including mission, scope, service model, phased capability build, and measures of success.
* Design the organizational structure, roles, and resourcing plan; recruit, onboard, develop, and lead a high-performing team of central laboratory technical and operational experts.
* Establish the central laboratory operating model and oversight framework, including standards, decision rights (RACI), governance forums, escalation pathways, and interfaces with Clinical Operations, Translational Medicine, Translational Biomarkers and Bioanalytics, Data Management, Biometrics, Quality, and Procurement.
* Develop the foundational processes, SOPs, work instructions, templates, and training needed to standardize central laboratory startup, conduct, and closeout across studies, and transition existing study-level central laboratory activities into the new group without disruption to ongoing studies.
* Develop the business case, budget, and resource forecasts for the group, and secure leadership alignment and sponsorship for the phased build-out.
* Lead the central laboratory vendor strategy, including evaluation, selection, and qualification of central laboratories and will consult in evaluation and selection of specialty laboratories as appropriate, technical capability assessments, quality and compliance reviews, contracting input with Procurement, service-level expectations, KPIs, issue escalation, and ongoing vendor governance.
* Provide technical oversight during clinical development planning and protocol design by assessing laboratory feasibility, test menus, specimen requirements, reference ranges, turnaround times, and the operational impact of study endpoints and schedules.
* Establish central laboratory systems and data capabilities, including laboratory information management systems, electronic data capture interfaces, data transfer specifications, edit checks, result reconciliation, traceability, and data readiness for analysis, database lock, and regulatory submission.
* Build quality and regulatory compliance into the group from inception, including ICH-GCP, applicable GCLP principles, CLIA/CAP or equivalent laboratory requirements, data integrity, inspection readiness, audits, deviations, CAPAs, and vendor change controls. Lead IVDR requirements for each protocol.
* Establish portfolio-level central laboratory metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting for quality, timeliness, cost, risk, capacity, data delivery, and vendor performance; use trends and root-cause analysis to drive risk mitigation and sustained improvement.
* Drive modernization through standardized processes, automation, digital integration, data analytics, and emerging laboratory technologies as the group matures.

**Sample Management Group Oversight**

* Provide leadership of the Sample Management group, including setting priorities, allocating resources, approving goals, and supporting talent development; day-to-day sample management execution remains with the Sample Management lead.
* Define the handoffs between central laboratory operations and sample management (e.g., laboratory manuals, collection kits, sample shipment to central laboratories) so roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths are clear.
* Ensure appropriate sample management resourcing and integration at the study level to ensure end-to-end sample mgmt support during study conduct
* Serve as the senior escalation point for sample-related issues that affect central laboratory testing, study timelines, or data quality.

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, COMPETENCIES AND SKILLS

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Clinical Laboratory Science, Biomedical Science, Pharmacy, or a related field; advanced

degree such as MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent is preferred.

* 10+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, central laboratory, diagnostic laboratory, or other regulated life-

sciences environment, with significant leadership responsibility for global clinical laboratory delivery.

* Proven track record of building a new function, team, or capability from the ground up, including defining strategy, operating

model, organizational design, processes, and governance.

* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including recruiting, developing, and managing teams and overseeing managers in

a matrixed global environment.

* Strong technical knowledge of central and specialty laboratory operations, service models, test menus, analytical platforms,

specimen requirements, reference intervals, laboratory workflow controls, and fit-for-purpose testing within clinical

development.

* Experience selecting, qualifying, contracting with, and governing global central laboratory vendors, including KPI/SLA

management, issue escalation, audits, CAPAs, and continuous improvement.

new_roles.description:
**Overview**

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Engineering, Procurement, & Construction (EPC) **Regional Commissioning Director,** you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 **Responsibilities** 

* Lead regional commissioning strategy and execution across multiple EPC datacenter projects, managers, vendors, and delivery partners.
* Manage and develop commissioning leaders, building team capability, succession depth, performance accountability, and consistent regional operating rhythms.
* Set regional commissioning priorities, governance, standards, and delivery expectations to ensure reliable, safe, and predictable turnover to Operations.
* Drive alignment across EPC, Engineering, Construction, Operations, Security, Procurement, and vendor leadership to resolve systemic risks and accelerate delivery outcomes.
* Oversee commissioning agent and vendor performance across the region, ensuring commercial accountability, quality execution, issue closure, and adoption of lessons learned.
* Monitor portfolio-level commissioning metrics, schedule risks, budget impacts, readiness gaps, and escalation themes, translating insights into action plans and leadership updates.
* Champion continuous improvement across commissioning standards, procedures, reporting, safety practices, and scalable delivery models for regional and global consistency.
* Embody our culture and values.

 
**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications**

* Doctorate Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years technical engineering experience
 + OR Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience
 + OR Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience.

**Background Check Requirements:**

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

* Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Doctorate Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience
 + OR Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 10+ years technical engineering experience
 + OR Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Reliability Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field AND 12+ years technical engineering experience.
* 4+ years people management experience.

There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $188,000 - $304,200 per year.

Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here:

new_roles.title: DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS JOB DESCRIPTION
new_roles.description:
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Directly Supervises: Executive Operations Coordinator, Administrative Manager, Administrative Assistants, Revenue Cycle Manager, Operations Manager, and other operational employees assigned by the Chief Executive Officer

Schedule: Full-time; 40 hours per week, with scheduling flexibility based on operational needs

Compensation: As stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement

Work Arrangement: Primarily remote, with weekly on-site presence required at Elevation's Homewood and Matteson offices

COMPENSATION AND HOURS

* This is a full-time, salaried-exempt position scheduled for 40 hours per week. The employee will receive the salary stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement and is not eligible for overtime compensation.

* If time reporting is required for attendance, workload, leave, or administrative purposes, the employee must accurately record actual hours worked. Time entries do not change the established salary.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Director of Operations ensures that Elevation Individual & Family Therapy's administrative and operational functions are organized, accountable, compliant, and aligned with client-service and financial goals. The position reduces the CEO's involvement in routine operations by resolving matters within the role's authority, ensuring assigned work is completed, and presenting recommendations when executive approval is required.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

1. OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP AND STAFF ACCOUNTABILITY

* Set priorities, deadlines, performance expectations, and coverage plans for assigned staff across both locations.

* Conduct regular supervision meetings and monitor attendance, responsiveness, accuracy, productivity, professionalism, and follow-through.

* Review required reports and promptly address missed deadlines, repeated errors, unresolved concerns, and incomplete work.

* Provide training, coaching, written expectations, and documented corrective feedback; coordinate performance improvement or disciplinary processes with the Executive Operations Coordinator and CEO.

* Assign each operational concern to an appropriate owner, monitor it through resolution, and escalate only matters requiring executive, legal, financial, clinical, or regulatory authority.

2. ADMINISTRATIVE AND CLIENT-SERVICE OPERATIONS

* Oversee phone and voicemail coverage, new-client inquiries, intake follow-up, insurance verification, required paperwork, scheduling, check-in, and appointment confirmation.

* Monitor re-engagement, no-show and cancellation outreach, copay collection, approved payment-plan workflows, and records requests.

* Ensure administrative staff consistently follow approved scripts, workflows, response-time standards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.

* Oversee office calendars, room assignments, supplies, equipment, routine facility concerns, and administrative coverage.

* Coordinate with clinical leadership when an operational concern affects client care, provider scheduling, documentation, or referrals.

3. REVENUE CYCLE OVERSIGHT

* Directly supervise the Revenue Cycle Manager, establish performance expectations, review results, provide coaching and accountability, and ensure timely follow-through on revenue-cycle priorities.

* Hold the Revenue Cycle Manager accountable for routine billing operations and supervision of assigned billing staff; coordinate cross-department priorities and escalate unresolved financial, payer, staffing, or compliance risks to the CEO.

* Review reports related to claims, denials, payment posting, insurance follow-up, patient balances, accounts receivable, and collections.

* Ensure billing concerns are assigned, documented, and resolved within established timelines.

* Identify administrative or clinical workflow failures that contribute to denials, delayed billing, inaccurate balances, or lost revenue.

* Coordinate communication among RCM, administrative, clinical, and collections staff and escalate material payer, financial, or compliance concerns.

4. POLICIES, SOPS, AND EHR WORKFLOW IMPROVEMENT

* Identify processes requiring a written policy, SOP, checklist, script, workflow, quality check, or escalation procedure.

* Draft and update operational policies and SOPs with the employees and subject-matter experts responsible for the work; coordinate approval by the appropriate leader.

* Maintain version control, review dates, distribution, training, employee acknowledgment, and monitoring of approved procedures.

* Evaluate EHR and technology workflows for intake, scheduling, documentation tracking, billing, records, client communication, and reporting.

* Identify duplicate entry, inconsistent data, preventable delays, and unnecessary manual work; recommend and coordinate approved templates, reports, alerts, tracking tools, automations, and vendor requests.

* Test approved changes, document the revised workflow, coordinate staff training, and monitor implementation while protecting confidentiality and system access.

5. HR, CREDENTIALING, AND COMPLIANCE COORDINATION

Directly supervise the Executive Operations Coordinator by establishing priorities, monitoring deadlines and accuracy, reviewing performance, and ensuring timely completion of assigned HR administration, credentialing, compliance, records, onboarding, offboarding, and policy-related responsibilities. The Executive Operations Coordinator or other assigned personnel retain responsibility for completing the detailed administrative work and maintaining required records.

* Ensure employee performance, attendance, conduct, onboarding, offboarding, training, personnel documentation, and policy-acknowledgment processes are coordinated appropriately and escalated to the CEO when executive authority or protected reporting is required.

* Review credentialing, recredentialing, payer enrollment, licensure, renewal, training, and compliance trackers; ensure assigned staff follow up on incomplete or at-risk items.

* Coordinate provider status changes with HR, billing, clinical leadership, scheduling, and provider-directory workflows.

* Monitor completion of corrective actions and escalate material delays, expirations, privacy concerns, payer or government inquiries, suspected fraud, client-safety issues, or other significant risks immediately.

* Support audits, internal reviews, payer requests, and corrective-action plans without acting as Elevation's attorney or sole clinical compliance authority.

6. BUDGET AND EXPENSE MONITORING

* Assist the CEO with preparing and monitoring approved administrative and operational budgets.

* Review actual operational expenses against approved amounts, including administrative and billing staffing costs, overtime, office supplies, software subscriptions, vendor charges, and upcoming renewals.

* Identify unusual spending, recurring overages, duplicate services, avoidable expenses, and practical opportunities for cost savings.

* Coordinate with billing and collections personnel to identify preventable revenue leakage related to denials, delayed claims, workflow errors, missed collections, or unresolved client balances.

* Maintain organized records of approved operational purchases and recurring expenses and submit purchase or budget-adjustment requests with the cost, purpose, priority, and recommendation.

* Provide the CEO with a monthly summary of significant budget variances, anticipated expenses, and recommended corrective or cost-saving actions.

7. REPORTING AND LEADERSHIP COLLABORATION

* Provide a concise weekly CEO report covering accomplishments, unresolved matters, staff concerns, revenue cycle issues, credentialing/compliance risks, budget concerns, and policy, SOP, or EHR project status.

* Provide a monthly operational summary identifying trends, recurring problems, performance patterns, completed improvements, and recommended priorities.

* Present significant concerns with relevant facts, actions already taken, and a recommended solution rather than forwarding unorganized information.

* Directly supervise the Administrative Manager and Administrative Assistants. Establish priorities, monitor performance, and maintain formal accountability while using the Administrative Manager's workflow knowledge and assigned functional ownership to support training, quality, office operations, and consistent administrative processes.

8. GROWTH INITIATIVES AND PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION

* Lead the operational assessment of CEO-directed growth opportunities, including new services, programs, partnerships, and location expansions. Work with clinical leadership, revenue cycle, and other relevant staff to assess demand, staffing, costs, reimbursement where applicable, space and technology needs, and implementation risks. Clinical leadership guides clinical program design.

* Present the CEO with a recommendation, estimated costs and resources, and a proposed timeline. The CEO decides which opportunities move forward.

* Lead the rollout of approved initiatives. Build the launch plan, assign responsibilities and deadlines, coordinate training and workflow changes, track milestones, and report progress and early results to the CEO.

ROLE BOUNDARIES AND DECISION-MAKING AUTHORITY

The Director of Operations owns operational follow-through but does not personally perform every task within the functions overseen. The position may assign and prioritize routine work, require status updates, provide coaching and corrective feedback, implement approved procedures, coordinate across departments, and resolve routine administrative or client-service concerns within established policies.

CEO approval is required before hiring, termination, suspension, compensation changes, material policy changes, unapproved contracts or purchases, new recurring expenses, significant balance waivers, banking or debt decisions, public statements, or substantive responses to legal, government, payer, or regulatory matters. The Director of Operations monitors and recommends but does not replace bookkeeping, payroll, accounting, or executive financial authority.

SCHEDULE AND CAPACITY

* Periodic on-site presence at both Elevation offices is required to observe day-to-day workflows, the office environment, staff performance, client-service operations, and implementation of policies and procedures. The timing and frequency of visits will be based on operational needs and CEO direction.

* The regular schedule will be established by the CEO and will generally total 40 hours per week. Some evening or weekend work may be necessary based on operational needs. The employee must maintain agreed-upon availability during core business hours for supervision, meetings, and time-sensitive matters.

* Continuous after-hours availability is not expected; after-hours contact should generally be limited to urgent matters that cannot reasonably wait. Occasional schedule fluctuations do not change the position's established salary.

* The Director of Operations must notify the CEO when workload or competing priorities cannot reasonably be completed within the established 40-hour schedule and recommend what should be delegated, postponed, or reprioritized.

* Unless otherwise approved, the role should generally carry no more than two major operational improvement projects at one time. Major launches count toward this limit unless the CEO approves an exception.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* At least three years of relevant operations, healthcare administration, office management, or employee-supervision experience.

* Demonstrated ability to supervise employees, address performance concerns, analyze operational data, and independently move work to completion.

* Strong judgment, initiative, organization, problem-solving, discretion, emotional maturity, and written and verbal communication skills.

* Ability to draft clear policies, SOPs, reports, checklists, and workflows and to protect confidential client, employee, financial, and business information.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Outlook, spreadsheets, cloud-based systems, and the ability to learn and improve EHR and business platforms.

* Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare confidentiality expectations; reliable transportation and ability to work from both Elevation locations as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, management, human resources, or a related field; behavioral health or healthcare operations experience; and experience with revenue cycle, credentialing, compliance, EHR workflow improvement, SOP development, reporting, dashboards, or automations.

new_roles.title: Director Destination Care Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**

The Director of Destination Care Operations drives the day-to-day operational success of CommonSpirit Health’s destination care program in partnership with clinical, financial, and internal and external stakeholders – serving patients traveling 150 or more miles for specialty care, from neighboring communities across the United States to international markets. The Director advances program performance, team excellence, and a concierge-caliber patient experience, ensuring every patient experiences frictionless care from first inquiry through return home. This role is suited to a self-driven leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong team leadership, process improvement skills, and comfort leading teams through change. The ideal candidate leads with adaptability, resourcefulness, and a collaborative spirit, and is deeply committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every destination care patient. This is an in-person, onsite role.

* Oversees the day-to-day operational performance of the destination care program, ensuring consistent and high-quality service delivery across all phases of the patient journey. Oversees referral intake and coordination workflows, ensuring timely and accurate routing, follow-up, and communication with referring providers and patients.
* Ensures patients, families, and referring partners experience seamless, concierge-caliber service from initial contact through post-discharge follow-up; conducts regular patient and family rounding to assess experience, identify service gaps and recovery opportunities, reinforce service standards, and gather patient stories that reflect the destination care experience.
* Delivers and ensures culturally informed service, communication, and care coordination across diverse domestic and international patient populations. Partners with clinical leadership and clinical advisory resources to support patient care operations and ensure the clinical needs of the destination care population are addressed. Identifies and leads process improvement and workflow optimization initiatives to advance operational efficiency, service quality, and patient satisfaction; develops and maintains operational protocols and standards that support consistent program delivery.
* Establishes and maintains documentation standards and data integrity practices across the team to support accurate program reporting, operational decision-making, and continuity of patient care. Serves as the escalation point for the team and provides availability for complex or time-sensitive situations as they arise. Manages the destination care program budget and is accountable for financial performance against established targets.
* Sets clear performance expectations, invests in professional growth, and builds and sustains a high-performing team culture grounded in service excellence, operational consistency, and continuous improvement; establishes clear standards and ensures consistent adherence across the team, addressing performance gaps directly and constructively.
* Oversees onboarding, cross-training, and workflow consistency across the program. Leads change management efforts within the team to support adoption of new workflows, service standards, and program initiatives.

**Job Requirements**

Required

* Bachelors Other Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field. and 5 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience managing and developing teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare organization, with direct accountability for program performance outcomes, upon hire and
* Experience delivering high-touch, patient-centered services for complex or high-acuity patient populations, including programs such as transplant, oncology, specialty referral, or equivalent tertiary or quaternary care settings, upon hire and
* Experience with electronic health record and hospital information systems; proficiency with productivity suites including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office., upon hire or

Preferred

* Masters Other Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Nursing, or a related field and 7-9 years 7 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience with international patient programs, embassy-sponsored care, or global sponsor coordination., upon hire and
* Clinical background including Registered Nurse (RN) licensure or equivalent clinical operations experience, upon hire and
* Experience in a dedicated destination care, international patient services, or specialty referral program at an academic medical center or large health system, upon hire and
* Experience building or expanding programs, including policy and operational protocol development, upon hire and
* Experience preparing and delivering financial and operating performance reports and presentations for leadership, upon hire and
* Experience with referral management, patient access, financial counseling, registration, or admissions workflows, upon hire and
* Experience managing program operations across multiple facilities or markets within a large health system., upon hire
* Certified Case Manager, upon hire or
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certification, upon hire or
* Project Management Professional, upon hire or
* Registered Nurse: TX, upon hire

Where You'll Work

Baylor St. Luke’s Medical Center is an 1,045 bed facility located in the Texas medical center. A joint venture with Baylor College of Medicine, Baylor St. Luke’s is an internationally recognized leader in research and clinical excellence that has given rise to breakthroughs in cardiovascular care, neuroscience, oncology, transplantation, and more. The hospital is home to the Dan L Duncan Comprehensive Cancer Center, a nationally-accredited and NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center. Our new McNair Campus is designed around the human experience—modeled on evidence-based practices for the safety of patients, visitors, staff, and physicians. The 27.5-acre campus represents the future of healthcare through a transformative alliance focused on leading-edge patient care, research, and education.

 **Pay Range** 
$60.24 - $89.60 /hour

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Strategic Operations for the Center on Reinventing Public Education
new_roles.description:
**Job Profile:**

Administrative Operations Manager 3

**Job Family:**

Administrative Operations

**Time Type:**

Full time

**Apply before 11:59 PM Arizona time the day before the posted End Date.**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

Bachelor's degree and seven (7) years of experience appropriate to the area of assignment/field including two (2) years managerial experience; OR, Any equivalent combination of experience and/or training from which comparable knowledge, skills and abilities have been achieved.
 
 
Job Profile Summary:
 
Administers and evaluates business and administrative matters within one department , including budget, operations, and programs and personnel administration.

**Job Description:**

**Salary Range** : $130,000 - $150,000 per year; offer dependent upon experience

 

The Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE), a leading source of transformative, evidence-based ideas about public education throughout the U.S., is seeking an experienced, strategic, creative, and detail-oriented systems thinker to serve as its Senior Director of Strategic Operations.

As a core member of the leadership team, the Senior Director will shape and lead the systems, processes, and operational strategies that enable CRPE to accelerate its national impact and internal effectiveness. This person will thoughtfully leverage AI, cross-functional collaboration, and relationships across Arizona State University to ensure CRPE operates and deploys talent most effectively as research, technology, and the education contexts change.

The Senior Director will oversee the strategy and execution of CRPE’s core organizational operations, including talent management, grant management, AI integration and adoption, and special projects. Working closely with the Center’s leaders, the Senior Director will ensure that organizational systems, policies, and practices support CRPE’s strategic priorities and reflect its commitment to a strong, inclusive staff culture. This role combines high-level strategic thinking and organizational design with hands-on implementation and problem-solving, designing systems and building the team that runs them.

The Senior Director will supervise a team of three and collaborate closely with other department leaders. CRPE is a remote team and is an especially strong fit for professionals who enjoy building effective systems, navigating complexity, and contributing to a fast-paced, high-impact organization.

**About CRPE**

The Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE) is a research organization at Arizona State University’s Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation, where transformative ideas are rigorously examined and tested, and research informs action. Since 1993, we have remained independent of any single ideology while holding firmly to our core belief that public education is a goal—to prepare every child for citizenship, economic independence, and personal fulfillment—and not a particular set of institutions.

From that foundation, we study what it will take for public education to meet every student’s needs and use those insights to inform meaningful changes in policy and practice.

Our current research explores four broad topics:

* **Students and Families** : We work to understand what students and families need from their education system—and how schools can rise to meet those needs.

* **Systems:** We examine the inner workings of schools, districts, and state governments, delivering insights into how our education systems work to meet the needs of students, families, and communities.

* **Innovations:** We identify promising initiatives outside the traditional education system that have the potential to radically improve teaching and learning, including artificial intelligence, new teacher staffing models, and district-wide innovations.

* **Politics of Change:** We study the critical role of politics in determining whether school systems deliver on their promise, and explore the ways public officials, school system leaders, and change-makers can factor political thinking into their strategies for improving education.

By partnering with the Mary Lou Fulton College, we are uniquely positioned to produce evidence and ideas that lead the country toward an education system that meets the needs of every student. Over the next five years, CRPE will produce ideas and evidence that inform effective state improvement, thoughtful AI policy and implementation, and innovative approaches to ensure every learner is prepared for a boundless future.

 

**Essential Duties:**

*Organizational strategy and change leadership*

* Partner with the CRPE’s Director and Managing Director to lead the organization strategically, helping CRPE adapt its organizational model, structure, and operations as strategy evolves.
* Translate strategy into implementation, turning priorities into operating plans with clear owners, timelines, and follow-through, and keeping leadership informed through coherent internal communications.
Own organization-wide staffing plans, capacity planning, and project resourcing in partnership with research leaders. 

*AI operational leadership*

* In collaboration with CRPE’s Research Principals, adapt roles, workflows, and tools for the age of AI, bringing in new technology where it improves research and operations.
* Lead AI integration across the organization, including policy and guidance, staff training and office hours, playbooks, piloting and scaling new uses, and building staff buy-in and tracking adoption.
Ensure staff have the systems, software, and equipment they need, and that data integrity, security, and records retention protocols are in place to adhere with University guidelines. 

*Talent strategy and people operations*

* Develop and implement a strategy to attract, retain, develop, and promote talent and support an inclusive workforce, drawing on a flexible mix of full-time staff, part-time staff, interns, and contractors.
* Lead CRPE’s annual performance review cycles, aligned with university requirements.
* Lead culture initiatives, including all-staff meetings, the annual staff retreat, professional development, and supporting staff and supervisors through feedback, to build a positive, respectful culture.
Supervise, coach, and develop a team of three: the People and Operations Manager, the Project Coordinator, and the Grants Manager. 

*University partnership manager*

* Serve as CRPE’s lead liaison and negotiator with ASU department leads, including HR, finance, sponsored projects, and IT partners. Find solutions within university systems and advocate effectively for CRPE’s needs.
Build collaborative relationships with other ASU colleges and units that advance CRPE’s mission. 

*Financial strategy and oversight*

Supervise and partner with the Grants Manager to oversee CRPE’s long-range financial strategy, including annual spending plans, multi-year forecasts, and funding and runway planning. 



*Oversight of special projects*

Lead or sponsor cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives that vary in complexity, urgency, and frequency as needs arise. 

 

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Master's degree in business, public administration, or a related field preferred.
* AI fluency and change leadership. Hands-on proficiency with generative AI tools and demonstrated experience leading organizational adoption of new technology, including developing policy, training staff, and building buy-in across teams with varied comfort levels.
* Talent and performance management. Experience designing and running recruitment, including coaching supervisors and managing contractor relationships.
* Complex project management. Experience leading multiple concurrent, cross-functional projects to completion amid shifting priorities and tight timelines. A track record of diagnosing operational challenges and building better systems.
Operations management. Experience overseeing financial and operational systems, including budget management and forecasting, grants administration, and human resources, in a nonprofit, education, or university setting (preferred). 

 

**Working Environment:**

* Activities are performed in an environmentally controlled office setting and involve extended periods of sitting, keyboarding, and use of a computer mouse.
* Position may require travel between campus locations or buildings for meetings or job-related tasks.
* Regular activities require the ability to manage and adjust to changing priorities, including handling time-sensitive tasks and resolving conflicts.
* MLFC supports flexible work options for certain positions, such as alternate work schedules and hybrid or full remote arrangements, subject to approvals per ASU policy.

**Department Statement:**

ASU’s Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation creates knowledge, mobilizes people, and takes action to improve education. Nationally recognized as a leader in teacher preparation, leadership development and scholarly research, Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation prepares over 8,000 educators annually. MLFC faculty create knowledge by drawing from a wide range of academic disciplines to gain insight into important questions about the process of learning, the practice of teaching and the effects of education policy. MLFC mobilizes people through bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs, through non-degree professional development programs and through socially embedded, multilateral community engagement. MLFC takes action by bringing people and ideas together to increase the capabilities of individual educators and the performance of education systems.

 

Aligned with ASU’s charter , MLFC is committed to advancing inclusive excellence in our curricula, programming and institutional relationships.

**Driving Requirement:**

Driving is not required for this position.

**Location:**

Campus: Tempe

**Funding:**

Grant Funded 

**Instructions to Apply:**

Current employees, student workers seeking staff opportunities, and students applying for student worker positions must apply directly through the Workday Jobs Hub .

 

To be considered, your application must include all of the following attachments:

* Cover letter
Resume or CV 

 

Multiple documents may be uploaded in the attachments section. Alternatively, applicants may combine all required materials into a single PDF for submission. Please ensure uploaded documents are clearly labeled and include your name.

 

Please ensure your resume includes all employment information in month and year format, for example 6/04 to 8/14, along with job title, job duties, and employer name for each position. Your resume should clearly demonstrate how your experience and background meet the minimum and desired qualifications for this position. Incomplete applications or missing required materials may not be considered.

 

**Important:** Do not withdraw your application to make edits. Once an application is withdrawn, it cannot be edited, reactivated, or replaced with a new submission. If you have questions or need assistance, please contact The Office of Human Resources Talent Acquisition before the posting close date.

 

Graduate Assistant, Intern and part-time positions are counted as half time for experience equivalency, meaning one year equals six months of experience.

 

Only electronic applications will be accepted for this position. By submitting an application, you confirm that the information provided is accurate and complete.

 

**ASU Statement:**

Arizona State University is a new model for American higher education, an unprecedented combination of academic excellence, entrepreneurial energy and broad access. This New American University is a single, unified institution comprising four differentiated campuses positively impacting the economic, social, cultural and environmental health of the communities it serves. Its research is inspired by real world application blurring the boundaries that traditionally separate academic disciplines. ASU serves more than 100,000 students in metropolitan Phoenix, Arizona, the nation's fifth largest city. ASU champions inclusive excellence, and welcomes students from all fifty states and more than one hundred nations across the globe.

 

ASU is a tobacco-free university. For details visit https://wellness.asu.edu/explore-wellness/body/alcohol-and-drugs/tobacco

 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by law.

 

**Notice of Availability of the ASU Annual Security and Fire Safety Report:**

In compliance with federal law, ASU prepares an annual report on campus security and fire safety programs and resources. ASU’s Annual Security and Fire Safety Report is available online at https://www.asu.edu/police/PDFs/ASU-Clery-Report.pdf . You may request a hard copy of the report by contacting the ASU Police Department at 480-965-3456.

 

Relocation Assistance – For information about schools, housing child resources, neighborhoods, hospitals, community events, and taxes, visit https://cfo.asu.edu/az-resources .

new_roles.title: Global Director, Supplier Quality
new_roles.description:
**Job Title:** Global Director, Supplier Quality

**Job Location:** Southfield, MI

**What we offer:**

VeoneerSafety Systemsis the world leader in Automotive Electronic Safety Systems. Veoneer’s scalable, best-in-class restraint control systems are mitigating the effects of a car crash. To date, we have delivered more than 1 billion devices to car manufacturers globally.
 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems has an international and collaborative team of 2,700 employees in 11 countries. We empower our people and are dedicated to their professional development and growth*.* 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems – Protect Everyone in Every Crash.

**What you'll do:**

The Global Director of Supplier Quality leads the global SQ organization, setting strategy, standards, and accountability for supplier readiness, performance, and continuous improvement.

The role combines global Supplier Quality leadership (80%) with North America Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leadership (20%).

**Key Responsibilities for Supplier Quality** (80% of role)

**Strategic Leadership & Global Deployment**

* Set global SQ strategy aligned with corporate, customer, sourcing, and manufacturing objectives.
* Define and execution of Supplier Quality Policies, Standards, Processes, Methods and Systems.
* Owner of Veoneer Supplier Manual (VSM), Supplier Quality Project (SQP) – APQP & PPAP, Supplier Non-Conformance Material (NCM) Management.
* Align cross-functional priorities, resources, and accountability; establish SQE oversight of workload, open issues, owners, overdue actions, and escalations.
* Monitor supplier quality targets, initiatives and indicators to ensure compliance to Veoneer Supplier Quality related policies, standards and reporting.

**Supplier Development & Standards Compliance**

* Oversee new supplier assessment, qualification, and development with Purchasing and Engineering; improve assessment models and ensure teams close risks and capability gaps before sourcing and production approval.
* Set common supplier requirements, risk-based audit and development expectations, and change controls; ensure existing suppliers improve capability and sustain company and customer compliance.
* Representing quality in Supplier Sourcing Board.

**Supplier Performance & Major Quality Issues**

* Lead major supplier escalations with supplier executives and cross-functional teams, ensuring containment, exposure assessment, production and customer protection, and verified permanent corrective actions.
* Drive common KPIs and improvement targets for supplier PPM, repeat defects, corrective-action aging, disruptions.
* Require leadership reviews and improvement plans for systemic issues, sharing lessons learned across suppliers.
* Supplier Scorecard (VS051 rating) and drive continuous improvement for supplier quality performance.

**Supplier APQP / PPAP & Safe Launch**

* Ensure on time and effective supplier APQP, PPAP, and Safe Launch for new programs, suppliers, and changes, including risk reviews, capability verification, and readiness-gap closure before production release.

**Quality Tools, Talent Development & Training**

* Set expectations for consistent SQE application of core quality tools, process audits, and structured problem solving to strengthen prevention and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Assess global SQ team capabilities and set development priorities with regional managers to strengthen technical expertise, expand skills, and build future leaders through training, mentoring, and succession planning.
* Supplier Quality talent review and succession plan.

**Regional Leadership: Engineering Quality & Operational Quality** (20% of role)

* Represent Quality Leadership team in regional activities across RDE, Manufacturing and Supplier Quality teams.
* Align regional priorities, governance, performance reviews, and escalations with global Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leaders and standards.
* Guide development and launch readiness, quality system execution, major issue resolution, and lessons learned while retaining local execution accountability.

**What you'll bring:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering.

**Experience:** Minimum 15 years in supplier quality, including supplier qualification, development, major issue resolution, and talent development. Electronics experience required; automotive SQ experience strongly preferred. Experience leading a multinational organization is preferred.

**Skills:**

* Global SQ leadership and effective matrix-team management.
* Cross-functional influence, supplier executive engagement, and timely decision-making.
* Strong supplier APQP, PPAP, change management, and Safe Launch knowledge.
* Advanced PFMEA, control plan, MSA, SPC, capability, audit, and 8D expertise; proven data-driven problem resolution and daily management.
* Strong commodity expertise for IC, PCB and/or mechanical parts is preferred.
* Ability to work effectively across cultures and time zones.
* Experience in other Quality domains is preferred

**Location:** Physical location Markham, Ontario, Canada or Southfield, Michigan; global scope across North America, Europe, India, and Asia.

**Travel:** International travel will be required 8-10 times per year.

**Reporting / Collaboration:**

* Reports to SVP Manufacturing & Quality.
* Solid-line responsibility for tech-center SQEs; dotted-line functional leadership of plant SQEs, with plant leadership retaining local operational accountability.
* Partners with Purchasing, Operations, Engineering, Industrialization, Program Management, and supplier leadership.

new_roles.description:

2026-11-13

**Country:**

United States of America

**Location:**

US-CT-EAST HARTFORD-OBG ~ 400 Main St ~ BLDG OBG

**Position Role Type:**

Hybrid

**U.S. Citizen, U.S. Person, or Immigration Status Requirements:**

U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are authorized to access information under this program/contract.

**Security Clearance Type:**

None/Not Required

**Security Clearance Status:**

Not Required

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

 

Pratt & Whitney is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power systems and has been revolutionizing modern flight for over 100 years. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

**What You Will Do**:

We are in search of a **17/24K Industrial Manager, Production Chief** who will be managing, reviewing, and approving Engineering Change Industrialization. The 17/24K Industrial Manager, Production Chief will be key team member within our 17/24K EC Industrial Team of the 17/24K Production Chief Office.

 

Reporting to the Deputy Production Chief, 17/24K EC Industrialization Associate Director, the role will be focusing on program management, industrialization of engineering changes, business process development, and detailed analysis to support program needs.

The 17/24K Industrial Manager, Production Chief will be instrumental in the achievement of Program milestones through alignment of Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain organizational plans and initiatives to Program and Customer priorities and commitments.

 

* Deliver executive presentations and program reporting on deliveries, risks, and industrial initiatives.
* Support communications, cross-functional alignment, industrial risk identification, and risk mitigation efforts for 17/24K programs.
* Participate in GTF PIPTs on behalf of the 17/24K programs.
* Collaborate with Mod Center, GSC, and cross-functional leaders on planning and execution of critical industrial actions to rate readiness for our programs.
* Leading continuous improvement activities to improve key processes; coordinate, organize, and lead critical industrial initiatives for engineering changes to minimize disruption to OEM and MRO operations
* Support MIPT and IPMT meetings for key engineering changes; present and align industrial content for critical customers
* Track and realign block changes for 24k program
* Champion MRL progression and productivity tasks
* Serve as the primary liaison for the Production Chiefs, ensuring effective communication and smooth execution across the PCIR process
* Partner closely with CAT 1 supplier to maintain alignment and drive successful incorporation planning
* Role involves travel up to 10%

**Qualifications You Must Have**

* Bachelor's degree and minimum 8 years prior relevant experience in an engineering, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement or related environment OR a Master's degree and minimum 5 years experience in an engineering, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement or related environment
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
* Experience working in a fluctuating environment with constantly shifting priorities
* Demonstrated ability to critically assess industrial production schedules, qualification requirements and develop risk mitigations to drive successful program execution.

**Qualifications We Prefer**

* Experience using SAP
* Knowledge of the PCIR process
Working knowledge of continuous improvement principles (e.g. lean manufacturing, CORE, QCPC) 

 

**Learn More & Apply Now:**

Please ensure the role type defined below is appropriate for your needs before applying to this role. This position is classified as:

**Onsite:** Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.

***As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote.***

The salary range for this role is 107,500 USD - 204,500 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills.Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement.Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance.This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply.RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window.

*RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.*

**Privacy Policy and Terms:**

identity_held_roles.title: Quality Director
identity_held_roles.description:
At Oceans Behavioral Hospital DeRidder, healing is our focus. We are passionate about helping adults and seniors manage the challenges associated with anxiety, depression and other mental health issues. Utilizing proven, innovative and progressive therapies, our qualified professionals strive to promote long-term wellness through a range of inpatient and outpatient psychiatric counseling and treatment options.
 
 
The Director, Quality and Patient Safety plans, develops, implements and manages comprehensive and effective systems to monitor and evaluate the quality and appropriateness of patient services and programs in support of the organizational mission and goals. This position will work closely under the supervision of the Hospital CEO, functions as a support person in the coordination and organization of administrative processes in a high quality efficient and cost-effective manner. All duties to be done in accordance with Joint Commission, Federal and State regulations, Oceans’ Mission, policies and procedures and quality standards.
 
 
**Essential Functions:**

* Works with VP, Quality and Patient Safety implementing organization-wide quality programs at the hospital level.
* Facilitates the hospital Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) committee.
* Prepares an annual evaluation of the hospital QAPI plan, including process and outcomes.
* Oversees hospital-wide performance improvement (PI) projects identified through on-going data driven quality assessment.
* Coordinates the hospital’s data collection procedures and provides on-going support and education to staff regarding QAPI tools and reporting requirements; utilizes data and collaborates with leadership to set priorities and provide guidance in their development of quality improvement work plans.
* Serves as a resource to the medical staff, administrators and other staff including participation in root cause analyses, as indicated, to investigate potentially avoidable sentinel events.
* Completes assignments accurately, in a timely manner and within procedural guidelines.
* Coordinates education for QAPI principles and regulatory standards as indicated. Conducts training for staff.
* Participates in Joint Commission Accreditation process including plan of action tracking and completion.
* Performs other duties and projects as assigned by the facility administrator and corporate office.

**Requirements**
**Education / Experience:**

* Associate degree or RN diploma required.
* Healthcare experience related to clinical leadership and/or quality assessment and performance improvement.
* Behavioral health experience preferred.

**Qualifications / Skills:**

* Demonstrates proficient computer skills with MS office products and electronic QAPI software solutions.
* Ability to create and provide training programs on related quality performance topics.
* Ability to work with minimal supervision and simultaneously manage multiple projects.
* Knowledge of state and federal regulatory requirements, Joint Commission Accreditation.
* CPHQ certification preferred.
* Must successfully complete CPR certification and an Oceans approved behavioral health de-escalation program.

**Work Environment:**
Subject to many interruptions. Occasional pressure due to multiple calls and inquiries. This position can be high paced and stressful; must be able to cope mentally and physically to atmosphere. Work requires spending approximately 90% or more of the time inside a building that offers protection from weather conditions but not necessarily from temperature changes.

identity_held_roles.title: Director, Quality Assurance
identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Director of Quality Assurance is a leadership role, responsible for all aspects of the Quality Systems, Clinical Quality and Manufacturing Quality for Aquestive. The Director of Quality Assurance will work with their direct managerial reports, as well as Executive Leadership, to ensure a continued state of compliance while promoting a strong quality culture across the organization for all products, spanning early phase development to commercialization.

This position will be expected to work in a highly collaborative, cross functional team environment, and provide expert knowledge to risk identification/mitigation, strategy and execution.

**Responsibilities:**

* Oversee all aspects of Quality Systems, Clinical Quality and Manufacturing Quality to assure compliance with FDA, EU, ANVISA, TGA and other international GMP requirements for all products manufactured at Aquestive (e.g., 21 CFR Part 210 + 211, EU GMP Volume 4 Part 1).
* Provide strategic direction and leadership to ensure effectiveness of Quality Systems (e.g., CAPA, Change Management, Event Management, Supplier Quality, Internal Audit, Document Management, Risk Management, Record Review and Product Disposition, Training, Field Alert/Recall, etc.)
* Lead and ensure execution of quality strategy for all development and manufacturing activities associated with all products manufactured by Aquestive, including external GMP contract manufacture operations or laboratories for drug substance and drug product.
* Primary contact for all inspection interactions with all domestic and ex-US regulatory authorities.
* Provide direction for escalated quality issues as they arise, determining the need for, and structuring communication for, further escalation to the Executive team and/or external parties.
* Lead strategic quality to quality relationships with business partners, suppliers, external CMOs and third-party testing laboratories.
* Ensure the company is upholding to Quality/Technical Agreements with business partners and suppliers.
* Provides input to all functions to ensure clinical trial activities are conducted in compliance with GCP regulations and internal requirements.
* Actively participate in the Site Leadership Team to drive continuous improvement activities and initiatives throughout Aquestive.
* Analyze, report and present metrics where applicable to show health of system(s).
* Lead GxP inspection strategies across all auditable areas to ensure the company is in an audit-ready status at all times.
* Manage overall coaching, training, development and succession planning for the function.
* Set, manage and monitor budget for Quality Assurance, in conjunction with finance.

**Qualifications:**

* Minimum of Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree in chemistry, engineering, biochemistry, or related science field desirable.
* Minimum 7+ years of related work experience working in a regulated GxP industry in pharmaceutical manufacturing operation setting or service oriented laboratory.
* Demonstrated ability to direct a function, oversee projects and teams. Minimum of 2 years overseeing direct reports.
* Minimum of 2+ years working in a managerial role with direct reports.
* Strong skillset in problem solving, strategic thinking, critical reasoning and decision making.
* Strong interpersonal skills and verbal/written communication skills.
* Excellent computer skills required (e.g., Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, Visio).
* Strong project management skills, strong organizational skills to maintain a high level of productivity, innovation, and priority-setting to complete assignments on time and on budget.
* Strong business acumen surrounding pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Some travel required.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the work being performed by colleagues assigned to this position. This is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Aquestive reserves the right to make changes to the job description whenever necessary.

As part of Aquestive’s employment process, final candidate will be required to complete a drug test and background check prior to employment commencing. 
**Please Note:**
Aquestive is a drug-free workplace and has a drug free workplace policy in place.

Aquestive provides equal employment opportunities to all colleagues and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

The Company is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the salary range for this job in certain states and cities within the United States. Final determinations with respect to salary will take into account a number of factors, which may include, but not be limited to the primary work location and the chosen candidate’s relevant skills, experience, and education.

Equal Opportunity Employer
 
 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws.
 
For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.

**Director of Continuous Improvement**

* **Director of Continuous Improvement**
* **Greater Charlotte Area**
* **$170,000 to $200,000 + Bonus + Strong Company Benefits**

A leading global industrial manufacturer is seeking a Director of Continuous Improvement to drive operational excellence, Lean transformation, and productivity improvements across multiple manufacturing facilities. Reporting directly to the C-suite, this high-impact leadership role will be responsible for deploying enterprise-wide continuous improvement strategies, developing Lean capabilities, and delivering measurable gains in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance. If you're passionate about building high-performing operations, coaching teams, and leading large-scale Lean transformations, this is an outstanding opportunity to make a lasting impact within a growing international organization.

**Key Responsibilities**
:

* Lead the deployment of Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement strategies across multiple manufacturing sites.
 
 Champion the use of Lean methodologies including Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, Standard Work, SMED, TPM, and Six Sigma tools.
* Support plant leadership teams in identifying and executing operational improvement opportunities.
* Coach and mentor Plant Managers, Operations Leaders, CI Managers, and Production Leaders.
* Develop Lean competencies throughout the organization through training, workshops, and hands-on coaching.
* Support facility footprint optimization, cost reduction programs, and operational strategy deployment.
* Pioneer the implementation of digital manufacturing and Smart Factory technologies.
* Ensure operational excellence principles are embedded into daily management systems and site culture.

**The successful candidate will ideally have**
:

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline,
* 10+ years of experience leading Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement initiatives within a manufacturing environment.
* 8+ years of experience applying Lean methodologies in high-volume industrial or automotive manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience driving measurable improvements in productivity, quality, and cost reduction.
* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB).
* Multi-Site Manufacturing experience

**Desired Skills and Experience**
\* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline,
 
\* 10+ years of experience leading Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement initiatives within a manufacturing environment.
 
\* 8+ years of experience applying Lean methodologies in high-volume industrial or automotive manufacturing operations.
 
\* Proven experience driving measurable improvements in productivity, quality, and cost reduction.
 
\* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB).
 
\* Multi-Site Manufacturing experience
