**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained

This role translates strategy into repeatable operating standards, disciplined execution, measurable performance, and scalable support.
  
  
The Director partners with field leadership and cross-functional teams to improve customer experience, delivery performance, carrier accountability, cost effectiveness, and launch readiness, enabling Regional Directors and market leaders to remain focused on field execution.

**Operational Planning & Routing**

* Develop, document, deploy, and audit routing standards that support safe, efficient, reliable, and customer-focused delivery execution.

**Operational Excellence**

* Lead the development, maintenance, communication, and adoption of standard operating procedures across Ashley Home Delivery.
* Design and continuously improve end-to-end processes for stand-up, load-out, route monitoring, check-in, returns, recovery, beginning-of-day controls, and end-of-day controls.
* Develop validation, compliance, and audit tools to ensure operating standards are understood, adopted, and sustained.

SHEIN is a global fashion and lifestyle e-retailer committed to making the beauty of fashion accessible to all. Founded in 2012, SHEIN has nearly 18,000 employees operating from offices around the world, with U.S. Headquarters located in Los Angeles.

In SHEIN, we work with outstanding, creative, and capable peers. We share an energetic and open culture for capable people to discern, work and ignite as a team.

At SHEIN, our culture is driven by our core values: Customer First, Take Ownership, Deliver Results, Make Change, and Celebrate Diversity. These are not just words, they are the principles that guide our work as we strive to meet the needs of our customers around the world.

**Position Summary**

As part of U.S. Fulfillment Operations, this director leads continuous improvement across SHEIN’s fulfillment center network. The role partners with site leaders and frontline teams to improve operating processes and management routines, owns the business intake and prioritization of warehouse system enhancements, and leads operational acceptance of system changes before deployment. The director works directly on priority initiatives and manages 1–2 direct reports.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Continuous Improvement and Standard Work***

* Own the network’s continuous improvement plan across receiving, putaway, inventory control, picking, packing, shipping, and returns. Use site observations, performance data, and root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks, defects, and process variation.
* Lead Kaizen initiatives with site teams. Pilot changes, verify results, and scale effective practices through standard work, SOPs, training, and process audits. Improve management routines for shift handoffs, KPI reviews, issue escalation, and corrective action.
* Set baselines and track sustained improvements in safety, quality, throughput, labor productivity, cost per unit, and on-time fulfillment.

***Warehouse Systems Requirements Management***

* Own the Operations intake and backlog for warehouse management system (WMS) and related tool enhancements. Consolidate requests across sites and prioritize them with Operations leaders based on impact, urgency, risk, and effort.

**Director of Quality**
=======================

**Colorado Springs, CO | Full-Time | On-Site**

### **Lead Quality. Develop People. Protect the Mission.**

At Cogitic Corporation, quality isn't just a department, it's critical to our mission. We manufacture precision components supporting the U.S. Navy and national defense programs, where accuracy, accountability, and reliability are non-negotiable.

We're seeking an experienced, technically strong Director of Quality to lead our Quality Management System (QMS), develop our inspection team, and drive a culture of operational excellence.

**This is not a desk-only leadership position.** We're looking for someone who can think strategically, lead confidently, and remain technically engaged. The right person is just as comfortable leading an audit or developing a quality strategy as they are reviewing a complex drawing, troubleshooting an inspection challenge, or supporting CMM programming.

If you're a quality leader who takes ownership, develops people, and believes in getting things right the first time, we want to hear from you.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

**Quality Leadership & Team Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Quality and Inspection team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and opportunities for growth.
* Build a high-performing team that values technical excellence, collaboration, continuous learning, and proactive problem-solving.
* Balance strategic quality initiatives with daily operational priorities to support production and delivery commitments.

**Quality Management & Compliance**

* Own, maintain, and continuously improve Cogitic's QMS, ensuring compliance with applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
* Lead internal, customer, supplier, and external audits, ensuring findings are addressed effectively and on time.
* Drive corrective action efforts, including root-cause analysis, corrective action implementation, and verification of effectiveness.
* Ensure quality processes support traceability, documentation accuracy, product conformance, and audit readiness.

**Technical Quality & Inspection**

* Oversee inspection planning, testing, and product acceptance for complex, precision-machined components.
* Apply advanced knowledge of engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, and dimensional inspection methods.
* Provide hands-on technical support with inspection processes, CMM programming, measurement techniques, and complex quality challenges.
* Maintain oversight of measurement and test equipment (M&TE), calibration programs, and inspection equipment readiness.
* Identify opportunities to improve inspection efficiency, accuracy, and first-pass quality.

**Cross-Functional Partnership & Continuous Improvement**

* Partner closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Mission Assurance, and Supply Chain to resolve quality concerns and execute customer requirements.
* Lead supplier quality activities, including qualification, performance monitoring, audits, and compliance with flow-down requirements.
* Establish and monitor meaningful quality KPIs to identify trends, reduce defects, and drive measurable improvements.
* Leverage ProShop ERP, quality data, and standard quality tools to strengthen processes, reporting, and operational visibility.
* Promote a proactive quality culture focused on prevention, accountability, and doing things right the first time.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, Welding Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum of 5 years of manufacturing quality experience, including hands-on machining, inspection, or precision manufacturing exposure.
* Demonstrated experience leading, coaching, and developing technical quality or inspection personnel.
* Strong understanding of AS9100 quality management systems, audit processes, corrective actions, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Advanced ability to interpret complex engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, and dimensional tolerances.
* Proven ability to investigate quality issues, identify root causes, implement sustainable solutions, and hold teams accountable.
* Strong technical aptitude, analytical judgment, communication skills, and ability to balance competing priorities.
* Proficiency with ERP systems, Microsoft Office, and technical quality software.
* U.S. citizenship and ability to successfully complete required background screening and meet applicable security clearance eligibility requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting U.S. Navy, NAVSEA, nuclear, or other highly regulated defense manufacturing programs.
* Hands-on experience with CMM programming, inspection planning, and precision measurement equipment.
* Experience managing calibration and M&TE programs.
* Working knowledge of ProShop ERP and SolidWorks or similar CAD software.
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), ASME GD&T certification, or comparable credentials.
* Experience with supplier quality management, customer audits, and complex contractual quality requirements.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

In this role, success means more than passing audits. You'll be expected to:

* Build a capable, accountable Quality team that operates with confidence and consistency.
* Maintain an effective, audit-ready QMS that supports the business rather than slowing it down.
* Reduce recurring quality issues through effective root-cause analysis and lasting corrective actions.
* Improve inspection efficiency, product conformance, and on-time execution.
* Develop stronger cross-functional partnerships and establish clear ownership of quality throughout the organization.

**Who Thrives at Cogitic?**
---------------------------

Our strongest leaders demonstrate our core values of **Performance, Character, Courage, Development, and Initiative.**

We're looking for someone who takes ownership instead of assigning blame, addresses challenges directly, coaches rather than simply directs, and understands that quality and operational performance must work together.

You should be comfortable in a growing organization where priorities evolve, expectations are high, and your leadership can make a meaningful impact.

**Compensation & Benefits**
---------------------------

**Compensation:** $150k - 200K annually, based on experience and qualifications.

At Cogitic, we believe in taking care of our team and providing opportunities to grow. Our benefits include:

* **Medical Insurance:** Competitive medical coverage with employer contributions toward premiums.
* **Dental Insurance:** Employer contributes 20% toward dental premiums.
* **Vision Insurance:** Voluntary vision coverage.
* **401(k) Retirement Plan:** Opportunity to save and plan for your future.
* **Life Insurance:** Employer-paid basic life and AD&D coverage.
* **Additional Coverage:** Voluntary life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability options.
* **Paid Time Off:** PTO and 10 company-observed holidays.
* **Professional Development:** Opportunities for continued learning, technical development, and leadership growth.

**Ready to Make an Impact?**
----------------------------

If you're an experienced quality leader who enjoys building strong teams, solving complex manufacturing challenges, and supporting work that matters, we'd love to connect.

**Apply today and help shape the future of Quality at Cogitic Corporation.**

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.

* Provide leadership across product and process quality, customer complaints, foreign-material controls, product holds, specifications, labeling, formulas, recipes, and Technical Services.

* Lead significant food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory matters with urgency, sound judgment, and appropriate escalation.

* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Research and Development, and Human Resources to strengthen ownership and accountability for food safety and quality across the business.

* Deep expertise in GMPs, HACCP, preventive controls, sanitation, microbiological risk, allergen management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recalls, supplier quality, AIB, SQF, and food safety management systems.

About Us

  

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

  

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

  

**Production leadership**

  

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

  

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

  

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

  

**Production testing and acceptance**

* Lead production acceptance testing and ground test operations.

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

* Support internal, regulatory and customer audits and certification activities.

**Growth and scale-up**

**People leadership**

You will be measured on aircraft delivery performance, production schedule attainment, factory throughput, labor productivity, manufacturing cost, quality and first-pass yield, safety, production-rate readiness, and workforce development and retention.

ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more.

We are seeking a hands-on Director to join our Strategy & Operations team and lead high-impact initiatives that improve how ShipMonk works across departments. Reporting to our Senior Director of Strategy and Operations, you will take our most important cross-functional problems from a blank page to a deployed solution: framing the problem, defining success, building the answer, and proving the results. Your first major initiative will be transforming how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse workforce.  
  
What you'll do:  
  
Lead Cross-Department Initiatives

* Lead major initiatives that improve processes across departments, especially where work, systems, and ownership break down between teams.
* Frame ambiguous problems, define the outcome, and work backward into a solution that teams actually adopt.
* Lead on-site discovery with leaders and frontline teams to understand how work really gets done.

Transform Workforce Management

* Lead the redesign of how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse teams, starting from what the business needs to achieve.
* Pilot solutions in one fulfillment center and scale what works across our network.
* Track the outcomes that matter, such as labor cost, staffing coverage, and retention.

Drive Continuous Improvement

* Help the whole organization work better, improving quality, speed, and the employee and merchant experience, not just cost.
* Spot recurring friction across teams, prioritize the biggest opportunities, and help teams adopt improvements that last.
* Make structured problem solving a habit at every level of the organization.

Strengthen Our Governance

* Support the organization as it matures how it sets priorities, makes decisions, and follows through on commitments.
* Partner with leaders to build governance practices that fit how each team works rather than imposing one structure.
* Bring clear analysis and decision materials to executive discussions.

Analyze, Build, and Drive Adoption

* Analyze productivity, capacity, cost to serve, and profitability, and build models that quantify trade-offs and turn decisions into action.
* Prototype tools and workflows hands-on with AI tools such as Claude, and partner with Engineering and Data to take them to production.
* Spend meaningful time on-site, leading change management so improvements stick rather than fade after launch.

What you'll need:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, supply chain, or a related field
* 3-5 years of experience in operations transformation, strategy, or management consulting, including leading implementations from requirements through deployment and adoption
* A track record of solving ambiguous, cross-functional problems with structured, KPI-driven thinking
* Experience leading process redesign and change management across departments; Lean, Six Sigma, or similar experience is a plus
* Strong analytical and financial modeling skills; SQL or BI experience is a plus
* A hands-on ownership style: comfortable on the warehouse floor and personally driving execution and adoption
* Experience building with AI tools such as Claude to prototype solutions
* Exposure to fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing operations; workforce management experience is a plus
* Strong executive communication and the ability to influence without direct authority
* Ability to travel 25–35%, with more time on-site during discovery and rollouts

**Our Core Values**

* **Merchant-first:** We handle the logistics so our merchants can focus on what they do best—growing their business.

**About Us:**

We are committed to finding smart solutions that enable an intelligent and seamless world. Our success as a world-class leader in technology has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. Our innovative sensing, connectivity, and motion solutions offer a diverse range of products across diversified end markets including transportation, medical, aerospace and defense, and industrial. We are at the forefront of supporting innovating life-changing technology, focusing on quality to keep people safe, healthy, and happy.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director, North America provides strategic and operational leadership for the regional manufacturing network, ensuring safe, compliant, cost-effective, and customer-focused execution across assigned sites. This position requires a hands-on, execution-focused leader who can standardize operating processes, improve performance variability across sites, coach plant leadership teams, and convert strategic business priorities into measurable operational and financial results. The Professor of Practice & Manufacturing Extension Program Director provides leadership for the Center for Manufacturing Excellence's (CME) manufacturing extension and industry engagement activities. The position connects University expertise, educational resources, faculty, and students with manufacturers throughout Mississippi and the region to strengthen organizational performance, workforce capability, operational excellence, and competitiveness. Working collaboratively with CME faculty and staff, industry, and economic and workforce development partners, the incumbent identifies industry needs and develops training, technical assistance, professional education, applied projects, and other services to address those needs.

  

The position will emphasize industry engagement, operational excellence and continuous improvement, applied problem solving, external funding, professional and graduate education, and measurable extension impact. **Position**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and day-to-day execution of manufacturing operations across three buildings within a large HVAC manufacturing facility. This position provides hands-on leadership to ensure the plant safely produces high-quality products on schedule, at the required volume and cost, while developing a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating production activities across multiple manufacturing processes and buildings, including assembly, sheet metal fabrication, welding, piping/refrigeration, testing, material flow, and final product completion.

The successful candidate will establish clear operating standards, drive cross-functional accountability, develop manufacturing leadership, remove operational constraints, and ensure the plant has the people, processes, equipment, and infrastructure required to support current production and future growth.

This position is expected to be highly visible on the manufacturing floor and serves as the primary operational leader responsible for translating business objectives into daily execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Plant Leadership & Operational Execution**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for manufacturing operations across all three buildings.
* Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating priorities aligned with business requirements.
* Ensure production plans are executed safely, efficiently, and according to customer commitments.
* Maintain strong communication and coordination between buildings and manufacturing departments.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability for production performance.
* Lead daily plant operating reviews and ensure corrective actions are completed.
* Identify and remove constraints affecting throughput, capacity, quality, or delivery.
* Maintain appropriate production capacity, staffing, equipment, and infrastructure to support business growth.
* Ensure standardized processes are consistently followed across all buildings.
* Maintain a strong management presence on the manufacturing floor.

**2. Production Management**

* Lead Production Managers and ensure effective management of production personnel.
* Establish production priorities based on customer demand, capacity, material availability, and schedule requirements.
* Ensure production schedules are achieved while balancing labor, equipment, materials, and testing capacity.
* Monitor production flow from fabrication through final assembly and testing.
* Develop and maintain effective production metrics and visual management systems.
* Identify bottlenecks and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Ensure appropriate escalation processes are in place when production performance is at risk.
* Coordinate production activities between the three buildings to maximize overall plant capacity.

**3. Safety, Environmental & Compliance**

* Establish safety as the facility’s highest operational priority.
* Partner with EHS leadership to maintain a strong safety culture across all three buildings.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, company requirements, and applicable industry standards.
* Drive accountability for safe work practices at all levels of the organization.
* Ensure timely investigation and corrective action following incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
* Support programs designed to reduce injuries, ergonomic risks, environmental impacts, and workplace hazards.
* Ensure employees receive appropriate safety training and understand their responsibilities.

**4. Quality**

* Partner with Quality leadership to ensure products meet customer, engineering, and company requirements.
* Establish accountability for first-time quality and defect prevention.
* Drive reduction of scrap, rework, warranty issues, and production defects.
* Ensure quality issues are rapidly escalated and contained.
* Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action processes.
* Promote quality at the source rather than relying on downstream inspection.
* Maintain compliance with the plant's quality management system and ISO requirements.

**5. Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the implementation and sustainability of Lean Manufacturing Principles throughout all three buildings.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement and employee involvement.
* Drive 5S, visual management, standardized work, problem solving, waste elimination, and flow improvements.
* Support Value Stream Mapping and improvement of end-to-end product flow.
* Establish measurable improvement targets for productivity, quality, delivery, inventory, and cost.
* Partner with Lean/Manufacturing Engineering leadership to prioritize improvement projects based on business impact.
* Ensure Lean improvements are sustained through management systems and standard work.
* Develop frontline leaders capable of independently identifying and solving operational problems.

**6. People Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Develop a high-performing manufacturing leadership team.
* Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Coach and develop Production Managers, Supervisors, and other manufacturing leaders.
* Identify organizational capability gaps and work with Human Resources to develop staffing and development plans.
* Support workforce planning and hiring activities necessary to meet production requirements.
* Establish effective onboarding and training processes for new employees.
* Develop succession plans for key manufacturing positions.
* Promote employee engagement, teamwork, ownership, and accountability.
* Address performance issues promptly and consistently.

**7. Capacity & Business Growth**

* Develop manufacturing capacity plans to support current and future customer demand.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Finance, Materials, and other functions to identify capacity requirements.
* Evaluate labor, equipment, floor space, testing, utilities, and infrastructure requirements.
* Support capital planning and justification for new equipment and facility improvements.
* Ensure new production areas and buildings are effectively integrated into the overall manufacturing system.
* Develop ramp-up plans for new products, programs, and production transfers.
* Ensure the plant can scale production without compromising safety, quality, or delivery performance.

**8. Cross-Functional Leadership**

Work closely with:

* Director of Operations
* Production
* Materials
* Production Planning
* Logistics
* Quality
* EHS
* Lean / Manufacturing Engineering
* Facilities
* Maintenance
* Engineering
* Finance
* Human Resources
* Supply Chain
* Sales / Customer teams

Ensure cross-functional issues are identified early, assigned to the appropriate owner, and driven to resolution.

**9. Facilities, Equipment & Infrastructure**

* Partner with Facilities and Maintenance leadership to ensure buildings, utilities, production equipment, cranes, test infrastructure, and other critical assets support production requirements.
* Establish preventive and predictive maintenance expectations.
* Ensure critical production equipment has appropriate contingency plans.
* Support capital equipment selection, installation, commissioning, and production launch.
* Ensure facility expansion projects are integrated into manufacturing operations with minimal disruption to production.

**10. Performance Management & Accountability**

Establish and maintain a plant operating system based on measurable performance.

Key performance indicators should include:

Safety

* Recordable incident rate
* Lost-time incidents
* Near misses
* Safety observations
* Corrective-action closure

Quality

* First-pass yield
* Scrap
* Rework
* Customer defects
* Warranty / quality escapes

Delivery

* On-time delivery
* Schedule attainment
* Production attainment
* Manufacturing lead time
* Test-bay utilization / throughput

Productivity

* Labor productivity
* Units per labor hour
* OEE where applicable
* Direct labor efficiency
* Throughput

Cost

* Manufacturing cost
* Labor variance
* Scrap cost
* Overtime
* Cost of poor quality

Lean

* 5S performance
* Kaizen completion
* Standard work compliance
* Improvement savings
* Value-stream performance

The Plant Manager will ensure performance is reviewed routinely and that corrective actions have clearly identified owners and due dates.

**Leadership Expectations**

The Plant Manager is expected to:

* Lead from the floor rather than from the office.
* Establish a culture of accountability without creating a culture of blame.
* Make decisions based on facts and data.
* Escalate issues early rather than allowing problems to become emergencies.
* Develop leaders instead of personally solving every problem.
* Maintain a strong focus on safety and quality while driving production.
* Create alignment between the three buildings rather than allowing them to operate as independent plants.
* Establish consistent standards and expectations across the operation.
* Communicate clearly with employees, leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Demonstrate urgency while maintaining disciplined problem solving.
* Build an organization capable of supporting significant business growth.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 3+ years of plant or multi-department manufacturing management experience.
* Experience managing large manufacturing organizations, multiple production areas, and facilities.
* Experience in HVAC, refrigeration, industrial equipment, sheet metal, welding, assembly, or related manufacturing strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing significant production growth or plant expansion.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience managing safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Experience developing and leading supervisors and managers.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environment.

Description:

LALA US Omaha Dairy manufactures yogurt smoothies and pourable sour cream. The facility provides a clean work environment, well-lit, highly automated production facility and career advancement opportunities. LALA US provides a competitive total compensation package including:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401k with company match
* Vacation and Personal time off
* 10 paid holidays
* Company-paid life, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
* Employee Assistance Program

The Plant Manager is a senior leader responsible for planning, directing, and controlling activities of a plant to accomplish budgeted operational and financial objectives. Directs all functions at the plant including production, quality control, finance, purchasing, inventory control, manufacturing, engineering, and employee relations. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, data-driven leader capable of scaling production capacity, optimizing labor efficiency, managing complex capital projects, and building a high-performing, engaged workforce.

This role is responsible for the achievement of all operational financial goals. The responsibility also includes establishing and managing operational policies and procedures, creating and maintaining a safe and quality-minded work environment, and fostering the development of a well-trained and motivated work force at all levels.

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. People leadership, talent development & labor relations**

* Recruit, mentor, and evaluate department manager, superintendent and shift supervisors, establishing clear accountability and succession plans.
* Foster positive employee relations, high retention, and strong shop-floor morale through transparent communication, town halls, and recognition programs.
* Manage collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and constructive relationships with union leadership.

**2. Production & operational execution**

* Direct multi-shift manufacturing operations to consistently achieve daily, weekly, and monthly production schedules and On-Time In-Full delivery targets.
* Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including Overall Equipment Effectiveness, scrap rates, yield, labor variance, and cycle times.
* Optimize production scheduling, capacity planning, and bottleneck management in partnership with Supply Chain and Materials teams.

**3. Financial management & P&L ownership**

* Develop, manage, and justify the annual plant operating budget, focusing on direct/indirect labor costs, raw material utilization, and overhead absorption.
* Track, analyze, and drive corrective actions on manufacturing cost variances, specifically Material Usage Variance, Labor Efficiency Variance, Scrap/Yield losses to protect margins.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain to investigate unfavorable material usage variances caused by Bill of Materials inaccuracies, machine calibration drift, or substandard raw materials.
* Conduct monthly financial variance reviews with corporate finance to identify cost-saving opportunities and mitigate inflationary pressures.

**4. Continuous improvement & operational excellence**

* Embed Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies (CILA, Centerline, 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, TPM, SMED) into daily floor operations.
* Lead cross-functional continuous improvement events aimed at eliminating waste, reducing changeover times, and improving throughput.
* Leverage Manufacturing Execution Systems and ERP data to drive predictive decision-making and real-time floor visibility.

**5. Environmental, health, and safety leadership**

* Champion a zero-incident safety culture by enforcing strict adherence to OSHA regulations, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, and company safety policies.
* Lead root-cause investigations for all near-misses, recordable incidents, and environmental excursions, ensuring timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
* Oversee environmental compliance, including EPA permitting, hazardous waste disposal, emissions monitoring, and sustainability targets.

**6. Quality assurance & regulatory compliance**

* Partner with the Quality Manager to reduce Customer Complaints, Cost of Poor Quality, and internal rework.
* Ensure the facility maintains strict compliance with industry quality standards (GMP, & SQF).
* Lead internal, customer, and third-party regulatory audits with zero major non-conformances.

**7. Maintenance, reliability & facilities management**

* Partner with the Engineering manager to achieve the goals on the Preventive and Predictive Maintenance programs to maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime.
* Ensure spare parts inventory management is optimized to balance carrying costs with equipment uptime requirements.
* Maintain physical plant infrastructure, utilities, security, and building compliance.

**Core Competencies & Attitudes**

* **Unbeatable attitude & resilience**: Maintains an optimistic, "can-do" mindset in the face of complex operational challenges, viewing equipment breakdowns, supply chain disruptions, and cost variances as solvable problems rather than roadblocks.
* **Passion for manufacturing excellence:** Brings genuine energy, pride, and enthusiasm to the shop floor, inspiring teams to take ownership of their craft and strive for world-class production standards.
* **Relentless focus on results:** Operates with a strong bias for execution and goal attainment, consistently driving teams to hit SQCDME targets and protect plant profitability.
* **Hands-on mindset:** Leads from the shop floor rather than behind a desk; actively walks the floor to observe processes, engage with operators, and solve problems at the source.
* **Extreme ownership & accountability:** Takes full responsibility for plant outcomes to engage the team can be focused on results.
* **Data-driven curiosity:** Approaches operational bottlenecks and cost variances (like Material Usage Variance) with analytical rigor, relying on root-cause data rather than guesswork.
* **Action & sense of urgency:** Responds swiftly to equipment downtime, safety hazards, and quality escapes while keeping teams calm and focused under pressure.
* **Servant leadership & empathy:** Listens actively to frontline workers, removes roadblocks for supervisors, and treats every team member with fairness and respect.
* **Continuous growth & adaptability:** Embraces change, challenges "*the way we've always done it"* and encourages calculated experimentation to improve efficiency.

**Core Soft Skills**

* **Multi-level communication:** Ability to translate complex operational metrics into strategic business updates for corporate executives, while communicating daily goals clearly and respectfully to frontline operators.
* **Conflict resolution & de-escalation:** Skilled at mediating disputes between competing departments and resolving shop-floor personnel conflicts calmly and fairly.
* **Emotional Intelligence:** Reads the moral and stress levels of the workforce, maintaining composure during crises like major line breakdowns, customer audits, or supply chain disruptions.
* **Cross-functional Influence:** Builds strong partnerships without direct authority over supporting teams to secure resources and align priorities.
* **Coaching & talent multiplication:** Focuses on developing future leaders by delegating effectively, giving constructive feedback, and empowering supervisors to make independent decisions rather than micromanaging.
* **Active listening:** Creates psychological safety on the plant floor so operators feel comfortable reporting near-misses, quality issues, or process inefficiencies early.
* **Stakeholder & customer relationship:** Represents the facility professionally during high-stakes customer visits, supplier negotiations, and community or regulatory inspections.

Requirements:

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Chemical), Operations Management, Supply Chain, or Business Administration.
* **Experience:** 10+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with at least 5 years in a Plant Manager, Assistant Plant Manager, or Operations Manager role overseeing 100+ employees.
* **Financial expertise:** Demonstrated experience managing a multi-million-dollar plant P&L, standard costing. Demonstrate understanding of managing budgets and controlling costs.
* **Systems proficiency:** Advanced working knowledge of SAP, MES platforms, and demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
* **Methodology expertise:** Proven track record of implementing Lean tools and driving measurable improvements in OEE, scrap reduction, and productivity. Working knowledge of Six Sigma, LEAN and/or Continuous Improvement principles, especially as they apply to a manufacturing environment

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration or master’s in engineering management.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification.
* Desirable food/beverage manufacturing plant operations experience, dairy experience strongly preferred

**Work Environment & Physical Demands**

* Split between an office environment and an active manufacturing floor with exposure to moving mechanical parts, varying noise levels, and temperature fluctuations.
* Requires regular walking/standing on the production floor and occasional travel (<5%) to corporate headquarters, conferences, suppliers, or sister facilities.

LALA US is an equal opportunity employer. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an at-will relationship.

Penn Aluminum is part of The Marmon Group, a Berkshire Hathaway Company. The Marmon Group comprises four autonomous companies consisting of 15 diverse, stand-alone business sectors and more than 185 independent manufacturing and service businesses. These businesses operate more than 350 manufacturing, distribution and service facilities, and employ more than 20,000 people worldwide.

Penn is investing over $60M in a state-of-the-art Murphysboro extrusion line that will double our tonnage output and open new markets, and this leader will be central to its success. * Strategic Planning: Partner with the President and executive team on long-term strategy, multi-site capacity planning, capital justification, and budget control.

* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

This position provides leadership and direction to approximately 30 employees, ensuring manufacturing operations are safe, efficient, productive, and aligned with company objectives.

The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader capable of managing multiple manufacturing functions, developing departmental supervisors, establishing accountability, and improving operational performance while supporting current production requirements and future manufacturing growth.

* Oversee daily operations and production performance across Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing.

existing_roles.title: Director, Protein Operations
existing_roles.description:
Twist Bioscience is seeking a Director, Protein Operations to lead high-throughput protein production and characterization within our Operations organization. You will run a high-throughput operation that runs seven days a week and lead a large, multi-level team that delivers purified, well-characterized antibodies and proteins to internal programs and external customers on time, at quality, and at cost. The ideal candidate pairs deep expertise in protein expression, purification, and characterization with the rigor to scale a production organization and the drive to automate it.

**Leadership and Operations**

* Lead a large protein production and characterization organization that operates seven days a week, including managers, supervisors, scientists, and associates.
* Own key performance indicators (KPIs) for quality, on-time delivery, turnaround time (TAT), capacity, and cost of goods sold (COGS), and model capacity and staffing against demand.
* Drive continuous process improvement and lead complex investigations, including customer incidents.
* Maintain SOPs, documentation, and training in line with ISO 13485 and other regulatory requirements.

**Protein Production**

* Oversee high-throughput antibody production in HEK293, CHO, and cell-free systems across IgG, Fab, scFv, VHH, and bispecific formats.
* Lead downstream purification of diverse biologics, including bispecific and engineered antibodies.
* Transfer new products and processes from R&D into production and support new product introductions (NPI).

**Protein and Antibody Characterization**

* Oversee Twist's binding, developability, and cell-based functional assay suite, from assay development through execution, analysis, and data reporting, with turnaround times as fast as 1–5 business days.
* Lead binding assessment, including flow cytometry on native antigen, single-point and full kinetics/affinity (KD) by SPR and BLI, and epitope binning by SPR and BLI.
* Lead developability profiling, including analytical size-exclusion chromatography (aSEC), thermostability (nanoDSF), size distribution (DLS), polyspecificity (BVP ELISA, ovalbumin off-target), self-interaction (AC-SINS), and hydrophobic interaction screening.
* Deliver high-quality, consistent datasets that support customer lead selection and AI/ML model training.

**Automation and Scale**

* Partner with Engineering to bring a high level of automation to production and characterization, translating workflows into requirements for liquid handling, robotics, scheduling, and data systems.
* Drive walk-away, high-throughput workflows integrated with LIMS, MES, and SAP to increase capacity, reduce turnaround time, and improve reproducibility.

**Collaboration**

* Partner with R&D, Process Development, Supply Chain, QC, QA, Project Management, and Customer Support to grow the portfolio and meet customer commitments.
* Shape technology and product direction with senior leadership while staying current on antibody discovery, protein expression, and lab automation.

### **What You'll Bring to the Team**

* PhD in protein biochemistry, biological chemistry, immunology, or a related field with 8+ years of experience in biotech, biopharma, or life science tools; or a BS/MS with 12+ years of equivalent experience.
* Experience managing managers and leading large teams, with strong coaching and people development skills.
* A proven track record of scaling protein or antibody production workflows and commercial products.
* Hands-on expertise in mammalian expression, purification (e.g., ÄKTA), and antibody characterization, including SPR/BLI kinetics and epitope binning, flow cytometry, and developability assays (aSEC, nanoDSF, DLS, AC-SINS, polyspecificity).
* Success partnering with engineering teams to implement automated, high-throughput lab workflows.
* Experience owning budgets, KPIs, and capacity planning, with working knowledge of ISO 13485/GMP, Lean, and Six Sigma.
* A strategic thinker who executes tactically, prioritizes well, and influences senior leadership.
* Excellent communication and presentation skills.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience running a high-throughput, made-to-order production operation in the life sciences.
* Experience manufacturing and purifying engineered antibodies.
* Experience with antibody characterization platforms such as Carterra and Octet.
* Familiarity with LIMS, MES, and ERP/SAP systems.

**About Twist Bioscience**

Twist Bioscience synthesizes genes from scratch, known as "writing" DNA. Just as children learn to both read and write, the next phase of development for the genomics revolution is the ability to write DNA.

At Twist Bioscience, we work in service of people who are changing the world for the better. In fields such as health care,agriculture, industrial chemicals and data storage, our unique silicon-based DNA Synthesis Platform provides precision at a scale that is otherwise unavailable to our customers.

**Director, Fund Operations**

**POSITION:** Full-time Exempt

**DEPARTMENT:** Impact Investing

**REPORTS TO:** Vice President, Impact Investing

**About the Organization**

**A FOUNDATION BUILT ON GREATER ATLANTA’S FUTURE**

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta is one of the nation’s largest community foundations, with over $1.7 billion in assets and more than seven decades of philanthropic leadership. Through grants, donor services, civic partnerships and impact investments, CFGA advances equity and opportunity across 23 counties in the Greater Atlanta region.

**The Role**

**BUILDING THE OPERATING FOUNDATION FOR IMPACT INVESTING**

The Director of Fund Operations will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s impact investing fund platform. This role is responsible for strengthening and scaling the systems, processes, infrastructure, and controls necessary to support a growing and sophisticated investment portfolio. This person owns the end-to-end operating model for the Foundation's impact investment platform. This is a senior, hands-on role responsible for making sure that once an investment is approved, it closes, funds, is serviced and is reported on correctly, on time and with a clear record. The work spans closing, funding, servicing, fund administration, compliance, records, data and reporting. This role supports every fund and vehicle on the platform — including the GoATL Community Capacity Fund, GoATL Affordable Housing Fund, TogetherATL Affordable Housing Fund, GoATL Community Guarantee Pool, and the Atlanta Affordable Housing Fund — together with related joint ventures and special purpose entities.

In practice, this person is the platform’s operational backbone: the person who knows what each transaction and fund requires, organizes the people and documents needed to satisfy those requirements, maintains the authoritative record, anticipates deadlines and exceptions, and follows issues through to resolution. The Director does not practice law or make accounting or credit decisions. Instead, the role makes sure Legal, Finance and the investment team work together smoothly and that nothing falls through the cracks.

The Director works hand in hand with the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing, who sits in Finance. The Director owns the process and the operating record: deadlines, checklists, documents, vendor performance and the loan database. The Fund Accountant owns the books: the general ledger, fund financial statements, capital accounts, investor statements and audit work. The Director makes sure the right information arrives complete and on time; the Fund Accountant decides how it is recorded and signs off on the numbers.

The successful candidate will combine transaction discipline, financial fluency, legal-document literacy, systems thinking and persistent follow-through. This person must be comfortable moving between a closing checklist, a fund agreement, a late borrower report, a wire request, a reporting calendar and a vendor escalation without losing track of what the governing documents require or the record of what was done.

**Why This Role Matters**

The platform now manages more than 60 loans across multiple funds and vehicles and is preparing to deploy its next round of capital. It has outgrown a model in which staff fill each operational gap as it appears. This role will connect the investment team, Finance, Legal and outside providers into one way of working: smooth closings, consistent records, clear deadlines, and systems that hold what we know about each fund, relationship and investment, so that knowledge does not live only in people’s heads.

* Creates one accountable owner for the transaction and fund lifecycle after investment approval.
* Replaces informal handoffs and institutional memory with documented workflows, complete records, calendars, controls and escalation paths.
* Gives Finance (including the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing), Legal and Portfolio Management a disciplined operating counterpart while preserving their independent authority.
* Ensures outside administrators, servicers and specialists work as extensions of our own process, with the Foundation keeping ownership of its records and decisions.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

**Transaction Closing and Funding Coordination**

* Own the closing process from approval through funding and loan setup with the servicer, maintaining a complete checklist of approval conditions, legal documents, due diligence, signatures, funding mechanics and post-closing items. Because real estate deals fund on the day of closing, every item, including the wire request, must be ready before signing day.
* Translate investment approvals and term sheets into coordinated workplans for the deal lead, Legal, Finance and the Fund Accountant, Treasury, the borrower and outside providers; surface conflicts, gaps and sequencing issues early.
* Coordinate document production and review, signature processes, lien and lender-agreement requirements, organizational documents, insurance, required consents and other closing deliverables. Track legal questions to formal resolution by counsel.
* Confirm that every funding and wire request is complete before it goes to Finance or Treasury: required approvals are in place, the borrower’s wire instructions have been verified by a phone call, and two people are involved in every wire. Maintain the standard wire request form used for both closings and construction draws.
* Ensure each closed transaction is set up accurately and handed off to the assigned portfolio owner with final documents, payment terms, covenants, reporting obligations, draw requirements and key dates recorded in the system of record under the loan’s ID.
* Give the Fund Accountant the final executed terms, funded amounts and key dates for each closing, so the loan is set up in the books from the same record.

**Fund and Entity Operations**

* Manage operating calendars and workflows for each fund, entity and capital source, including capital calls, distributions, investor onboarding, bank account administration (account openings and authorized signers), subscriptions, side letters, governance actions and record retention. The Fund Accountant calculates investor allocations, capital accounts and distribution amounts and records them; this role runs the calendar, notices and documents around them.
* Own a single, current investor contact list, including financial advisors and fund administrator portal access, so that capital call notices, reports and distributions reach the right people.
* Maintain one register of what each fund is required to do under its governing agreements, side letters, policies, approval authorities and committee actions; coordinate implementation with the accountable business, Legal and Finance owners.
* Track state filings, annual report deadlines and registered-agent requirements across all entities, and support General Counsel as needed in preparing and completing these filings. General Counsel owns legal and state filings and Finance owns tax and regulatory filings; this role keeps one shared calendar for all of them.
* Support cash forecasting and liquidity planning by giving the Fund Accountant and the Vice President, Impact Investing expected closing, draw and repayment dates, while preserving Finance's authority over cash, treasury policy and accounting treatment.
* Support Finance-led annual audits and tax work by gathering key information and answering common requests. The Fund Accountant manages the audit and the auditor relationship, and Finance keeps ownership of audit and tax strategy, filings and sign-off. Organize valuations and other fund-level deliverables by assembling source materials, tracking deadlines, coordinating responses and driving open items to resolution.

**Servicing and Portfolio Operations**

* Own the operational relationship with loan servicers and administrators, including billing, payment processing, notices, escrows, statements, payoff calculations, deadline reminders and follow-up on exceptions.
* Ensure payments, draws, amendments, waivers, modifications and payoff activity are documented, routed and recorded consistently. Escalate issues that stay unresolved and any service failures.
* Run the quarterly borrower reporting process: track whether each report has arrived and is complete, send notices when reports are late or missing pieces, and make sure reviewed figures are recorded in the system of record.
* Keep the calendar for annual affordability compliance reviews (rents, incomes and other terms required by each loan’s affordability restrictions) and loan maturities, so reviews by asset managers happen on schedule.
* Coordinate operational support for loans in workout or needing special attention, including document collection, approval tracking, counsel coordination and implementation of authorized actions.
* Distinguish operational monitoring from credit judgment: route substantive covenant, borrower-performance and risk matters to Portfolio and Asset Management and track resulting actions to completion.

**Data, Records and Reporting Infrastructure**

* Carry out the platform’s plan to move from scattered files and systems (including Foundant, SharePoint, Excel, the DocuSign data room, and the fund administrator’s Egnyte and Salesforce portal) to a single system of record, working with Investment, Finance, Legal, IT and the fund administrator.
* In coordination with IT and third-party partners, establish and maintain the system of record (a loan database) for fund, investor and transaction information, with clear ownership, access controls, shared IDs, naming standards and a full history of changes. Key terms lock at closing and change only through a dated, approved modification.
* Work with IT to build and maintain automated workflows (for example, in Power Automate) that move data between systems, send deadline alerts and refresh Power BI dashboards, and use AI tools to prepare summaries and checks for staff to review. Coordinate with the Fund Accountant so the loan database and the accounting records tie out.
* Own operational data quality and check that key fields match across closing records, servicing systems, administrator records and Finance systems; resolve any differences with the appropriate source owner.
* Maintain the master calendar for investor reporting, committee, board, audit, tax, compliance and portfolio deliverables and coordinate timely inputs from accountable content owners.

**Vendor Management and Process Improvement**

* Serve as the primary business owner for third-party fund administration, servicing, payment processing and related operational providers; set service standards, make sure the Foundation has access to the source records, and define how issues are escalated and when a provider can be replaced.
* Share vendor oversight with the Fund Accountant: this role owns the relationship, contract terms, service standards and timeliness; the Fund Accountant reviews the financial accuracy of what providers produce (interest, balances, investor statements and fund reports) before it is posted or shared.
* Monitor service performance, check that provider reports arrive on time and match the operating record (the Fund Accountant checks the financial figures) and lead resolution of errors, backlogs and control failures.
* Document and continuously improve workflows for approvals, closings, disbursements, servicing, amendments, reporting and record retention. Partner with the Fund Accountant where workflows touch the books, such as the monthly close; Finance owns accounting procedures and reconciliations.
* Design procedures that are durable, teachable and appropriately scaled rather than dependent on one employee's memory or heroics.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

* Manage any future operations or servicing staff; establish clear ownership, service expectations and backup coverage.
* Run recurring operating meetings that convert cross-functional issues into decisions, named owners and deadlines.
* Refine roles, responsibilities, workflows, and accountability standards across teams involved in fund operations and investment management.
* Raise issues promptly and concisely with the Vice President, Impact Investing and enterprise leadership (legal and finance) when service failures, unresolved legal or financial questions, capacity constraints or control gaps threaten a closing, obligation or relationship.
* Build strong working relationships across teams while being willing to insist on complete documentation, clear authority and timely decisions.

**Qualifications**

**WHAT YOU BRING**

**Required**

* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in fund operations, transaction management, loan administration, investment operations, structured finance, real estate finance, private credit, community development finance or a closely related field.
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, real estate, public administration or a related field required.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating transactions through closing and funding, including legal documentation, cash mechanics and post-closing requirements.
* Working knowledge of financial statements, loan and investment documents, entity and fund records, payment and servicing processes, reconciliations and internal controls.
* Ability to build, lead, and evolve operational functions within a growing or complex organization.
* Confidence in evaluating existing practices, constructively challenging the status quo, and driving meaningful process improvements.
* Exceptional project management and organizational judgment, with the ability to maintain accuracy across multiple vehicles, transactions, deadlines and stakeholders.
* Strong written communication and the ability to convert complex requirements into clear checklists, procedures, records and short, clear updates for leadership when something is off track.
* Experience holding internal and external partners accountable, escalating appropriately and following issues through closure.
* A clear commitment to CFGA’s mission of equity and shared prosperity for all.

**Preferred**

* Experience with affordable housing, community development lending, program-related investments, impact investing or philanthropic investment vehicles.
* Experience managing a third-party fund administrator, loan servicer, closing counsel, tax provider or comparable outsourced operating partner.
* Experience building or improving an operating model, system of record, compliance calendar or reporting infrastructure.
* Comfort with Microsoft 365 tools such as SharePoint, Lists, Power Automate and Power BI; loan or relationship management systems such as Foundant or Salesforce; and tools used to summarize and check documents.
* Masters degree in relevant field.
* Relevant legal-operations, paralegal, fund-administration or project-management training is valuable; a law degree or CPA is not required.

**HYBRID SCHEDULE**

The Community Foundation operates in a hybrid working environment with staff working in-office three days per week and the opportunity to work two days remotely per week if in good standing.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is

$130,000 - $150,000. This position is exempt and eligible for the Foundation’s competitive health and benefits plan, which includes:

**TO APPLY**
